name: Medium Blue
lede: Medium Blue is a pure, saturated blue, one of the named colors of the web.

sections.title: A web color
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary lists MediumBlue as one of the colours in the X11 color set, with the hex code #0000CD [1]. That is the whole of its pedigree: a label in a software list, placed between the darker blues and the lighter ones. Our records also list it in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system [2].

The phrase also has an older, plain meaning. Paterson uses it for stone blue [3], and Pastoureau notes that the azur of French royal arms could be sky blue, medium blue or ultramarine, with no difference of meaning, since artists were free to choose [4]. Gage quotes an old list of color terms that calls lapis lazuli a blue-black, adding that some say it is a medium blue [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering as much as 1% of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes the archive, not painting as a whole: this is a pure screen blue, much more intense than most painted blues. Related names: [[blue]], [[royal-blue]], [[cobalt-blue]] and [[azure]].
